title: Fibrant pullback invariance detected by simplicial mapping spaces
statement: Use simplicial model categories, cofibrant and fibrant objects, weak equivalences, Kan mapping sets and $\mathcal C=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{cf}})$ as in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicial model category in which every object is cofibrant. Let $U,U',E$ be fibrant objects, let $a:U\to U'$ be a weak equivalence, and let $b:E\to U'$ be a fibration. Let $D=U\times_{U'}E$ be the strict pullback and $h:D\to E$ its projection. Then $D$ is fibrant, and for every bifibrant object $T$ the induced map of enriched simplicial mapping sets $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(T,D)\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(T,E)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. Consequently the edge of $\mathcal C$ represented by $h$ is an equivalence. No right properness hypothesis is imposed on $\mathcal M$. All objects and mapping spaces are taken in fixed containing universes.

source.place: Remark A.2.4.5 (fibrant-object alternative to right properness), with the simplicial mapping-space proof of pullback invariance between fibrant objects Agent formulation of the supporting argument; read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. proof.text: Write $r:D\to U$ for the other pullback projection. Fibrations have the right lifting property against trivial cofibrations by [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. A lifting square against $r$ gives one against $b$ after composing its bottom map with $a$; the lift against $b$, paired with the original bottom map to $U$, gives a lift to $D$ by the pullback property. Thus $r$ is a fibration. Right lifting properties are closed under composition (first lift against the second map, then against the first), so $D\xrightarrow r U\to1$ is a fibration. Hence $D$ is fibrant. The all-cofibrant hypothesis makes $D,E,U,U\prime$ bifibrant.

source.place: Remark A.2.4.5; explicit elementary lifting argument for fibrancy.

proof.text: Fix a bifibrant $T$ and write $M_T(X)=\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(T,X)$. The tensor adjunction [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor] identifies its $n$-simplices with ordinary maps $\Delta^n\otimes T\to X$. Consequently $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(T,1)$ is the point, and $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(0,X)$ is the point: $\Delta^n\otimes-$ is a left adjoint, hence preserves the initial object. Apply the mapping-space axiom of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] to $0\to T$ and each fibrant terminal map $X\to1$. It gives that $M_T(D),M_T(E),M_T(U),M_T(U\prime)$ are Kan. Applied instead to $0\to T$ and $b$, the same axiom says that $M_T(b):M_T(E)\to M_T(U\prime)$ is a Kan fibration.

source.place: Appendix A.3.1, simplicial model axiom, specialized to an initial cofibration.

proof.text: Let $q$ be the infinity localization of $\mathcal M$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. By [def-coef-coherent-localization-interface], $q(a)$ is an equivalence edge, since $a$ is a weak equivalence; let $g:qU'\to qU$ be an inverse. By Step 1, $U$ and $U'$ are bifibrant. The former node's representation clause, applied to $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(U',U)$, is a bijection on path components onto morphisms $qU'\to qU$ up to homotopy; choose a vertex $a':U'\to U$ in the component representing $g$. Since the comparison respects compositions and $q$ sends identities to identities, $aa'$ lies in the path component of $1_{U'}$ in $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(U',U')$, and $a'a$ in that of $1_U$ in $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(U,U)$; both are Kan by Step 2 with $T=U'$, $T=U$. In a Kan complex one component is joined by a single edge (reverse by an outer two-horn, compose by an inner one); take $\gamma:\Delta^1\to\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(U',U')$ from $1_{U'}$ to $aa'$. Enriched composition $\Delta^1\times M_T(U')\xrightarrow{\gamma\times1}\underline{\operatorname{Map}}(U',U')\times M_T(U')\to M_T(U')$ is a simplicial homotopy from the identity to $M_T(a)M_T(a')$; likewise $M_T(a')M_T(a)$ is homotopic to the identity. By [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], $|\Delta^1\times K|\cong[0,1]\times|K|$, so the realizations are homotopy inverse. A homotopy equivalence is bijective on path components and on homotopy groups at every basepoint. Thus $M_T(a):M_T(U)\to M_T(U')$ is a weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes.

source.place: Remark A.2.4.5, reconstructed mapping-space argument; a representative of the inverse of q(a) and enriched-composition homotopies.

proof.text: The tensor adjunction [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor] identifies the $n$-simplices of $M_T(D)$ with maps $\Delta^n\otimes T\to D$. The defining pullback property identifies these, bijectively, with pairs of maps $\Delta^n\otimes T\to U$ and $\Delta^n\otimes T\to E$ whose composites to $U\prime$ agree. This identification commutes with every simplex operator by precomposition, so it is an isomorphism of simplicial sets $$M_T(D)=M_T(U)\times_{M_T(U\prime)}M_T(E).$$ Under this identification $M_T(h)$ is the second projection; hence it is precisely the pullback of $M_T(a)$ along $M_T(b)$.

source.place: Remark A.2.4.5; elementary degreewise calculation using the tensor adjunction and the strict pullback.

proof.text: By Steps 2 and 3, $M_T(b)$ is a Kan fibration and $M_T(a)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The right-properness clause of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core] applies to this square of simplicial sets. Together with Step 4 it gives that $M_T(h)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 2 already established that its source and target are Kan. Since $T$ was arbitrary, this proves the asserted mapping-space clause. Right properness has been used only for simplicial sets, not for $\mathcal M$.

source.place: Remark A.2.4.5; Kan right properness as supplied by Hovey Theorem 3.6.5.

proof.text: Both $E$ and $D$ are bifibrant by Step 1, so they may serve as $T$. Surjectivity on components for $M_E(h)$ supplies a vertex $k:E\to D$ with $[hk]=[1_E]$. Precomposing this equality with $h:D\to E$ gives $[hkh]=[h]$. Injectivity on components for $M_D(h)$ then gives $[kh]=[1_D]$. These are component equalities in Kan mapping sets. Each can be witnessed by one edge in the direction from the identity to the composite: reverse an edge by filling an outer two-horn, and combine successive edges by filling an inner two-horn. In the explicit coherent nerve of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], such an edge is exactly a two-simplex with its direct edge the identity and its two other edges $h,k$ (or $k,h$), because the $0$-to-$2$ mapping set of the thickened $[2]$ is $\Delta^1$. These two triangles exhibit $k$ as a two-sided inverse to the edge represented by $h$, which is the definition of equivalence in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Remark A.2.4.5; explicit inverse test using the coherent-nerve definition and Kan horns.

lean.statement: theorem fibrant_pullback_mapping_invariance (M : Type u) [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization (cofibrations M) (trivialFibrations M)] [MorphismProperty.HasFunctorialFactorization (trivialCofibrations M) (fibrations M)] [SimplicialCategory M] (_tensor : SimplicialTensorCotensor M) (_sm7 : SimplicialModelLocalization.SatisfiesSM7 M) (_allCofibrant : ∀ X : M, IsCofibrant X) (U U' E : M) [IsFibrant U] [IsFibrant U'] [IsFibrant E] (a : U ⟶ U') [WeakEquivalence a] (b : E ⟶ U') [Fibration b] : IsFibrant (pullback a b) ∧ (∀ T : M, IsCofibrant T → IsFibrant T → SSet.KanComplex (sHom T (pullback a b)) ∧ SSet.KanComplex (sHom T E) ∧ SSet.Enhanced.IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (eHomWhiskerLeft SSet T (pullback.snd a b))) ∧ ∃ e : (SimplicialNerve (SimplicialModelLocalization.Bif M)) _⦋1⦌, (e.obj (.mk (ULift.up 0))).obj = pullback a b ∧ (e.obj (.mk (ULift.up 1))).obj = E ∧ HEq (e.map (.mk (ULift.up 0)) (.mk (ULift.up 1))) (SSet.const (homEquiv' (pullback a b) E (pullback.snd a b)) : sHom (SimplicialThickening.mk (ULift.up.{v, 0} (0 : Fin 2))) (SimplicialThickening.mk (ULift.up.{v, 0} (1 : Fin 2))) ⟶ sHom (pullback a b) E) ∧ SSet.Enhanced.IsEquivalenceEdge (SimplicialNerve (SimplicialModelLocalization.Bif M)) e
lean.note: The final existential specifies the actual coherent edge by its underlying source and target objects and its entire enriched map as the constant map at the strict pullback projection. These equations determine the edge uniquely, so no unrelated equivalence edge can witness the conclusion.
